messages:
jon: quick dump from early-morning perf sweep — noticed a regression in tokens/sec for small-batch, low-KV-hit workloads. numbers below from the staging G10 run.
jon: raw summary (seq=256): FlashV1: 2000 tok/s, FusedAttn: 1600 tok/s, PagedAttn: 1900 tok/s. GPU cost ~= $3/hr on this pool.
jon: translated to $/M tokens: FlashV1 ~ $0.42, Fused ~ $0.52, Paged ~ $0.44. that delta matters at scale for small customers.
perf-bot: automated profile attached: kernel-switch events ↑10% on fallback path, kv-cache miss ratio correlated with FusedAttn slowdowns.
amy: interesting — is the regression triggered by eviction/kv-reload spikes? or purely kernel-choice overhead?
jon: looks like both. when KV hit < 0.6 we see more paging and a higher variance in per-token latency; kernel selection sometimes picks Fused because of memory footprint heuristics, but fused loses on small batches.
ravi: can you paste the perf command and the small trace? want to reproduce locally.
jon: repro command: ```python tools/bench_tokens.py --model redwood-3b --kernel auto --batch 4 --seq 256 --kv-hit 0.5 --runs 20 --log perf/1860001234.log```
jon: snippet from perf log: ```median_latency_per_token_ms: FlashV1=0.50, Fused=0.63, Paged=0.53; p95: FlashV1=1.1, Fused=1.8, Paged=1.2; kernel_switch_count=42```
sarah: maybe we need a short-circuit: if batch_size <= 8 and kv_hit < 0.7 prefer FlashV1, else allow Fused. That reduces $/M by ~8% for this workload.
amy: agree but watch memory pressure — FlashV1 uses more peak mem for long seqs. add an override: if seq > 1024 force paged/fused.
ravi: propose a lightweight policy proto: ```policy: if seq<=512 and batch<=8 and kv_hit<0.7 -> kernel=FlashV1 elif seq<=512 and batch>8 -> kernel=PagedAttn else kernel=FusedAttn```
jon: also add hysteresis so we don't flip per-request. consider a 30s windowed avg kv_hit and batch distribution.
sarah: on rollout, we can A/B 5% -> 20% with token-metered cost monitoring. set alert if tokens/sec drop >7% or $/M increase >5%.
perf-bot: note: added a regression alert rule in staging for this thread id; will fire if p95 increases by >25% for the canary group. :bell:
amy: I'll implement the policy as a config flag under runtime/kernel_selector and add unit tests for the kv_hit calc.
ravi: I'll run a sweep across seq lengths (128/256/512/1024) and batch sizes (1/4/8/16) and push results to perfdb.
jon: thanks — saved the initial logs to perf/1860001234/ and uploaded a small csv with tokens/sec and cost calc. tagging @product when we have a clear $/M delta.
sarah: small note: include cold-start where kv-cache empty — that flips the numbers; we should weight cold-start cost in our heuristics.
jon: agreed. next update after sweep (iming: today EOD).
